Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Objective 2 Gameplay 3 List of Donuts 3.1 2 Players 3.2 3 Players 3.3 4 Players 3.4 5 to 6 Players Objective Get as many donuts as you can to score the highest score at the end of the game. Gameplay A game consists of several rounds. At the start of a round, refill the donut row up to the number of players plus 1. Each player secretly bids on a donut card by choosing the number card that matches the donut they wish to bid on. Then, everyone reveals their cards. If a card is bid on by one person, they get it. If a card is bid on by 2 or more people, it is discarded. The cards are rewarded from lowest number to highest. (1 gets removed from the board first, then 2 gets removed, and so on.) When there are not enough cards from the deck to refill the row, the game ends and highest score wins. If there is a tie, the player with more cards wins. If there is still a tie, they share the victory. Important: You may only activate a card's power when you take it from the donut row. The power does not activate when you get the card from another player, draw from the deck, or take from the discard pile. List of Donuts 2 Players Chocolate Frosted (3): Immediately draw the top card from the deck and place it in front of you. Donut Holes (6): Score 1 point if you have one, 3 for two, 6 for three, 10 for four, or 15 if you have five or more. Éclair (3): Immediately take the top card from the discard pile. French Cruller (1 per player count color): Score 2 points. Also, discard any number of cards in the donut row that were not selected. Glazed (5): Score 2 points. Jelly-Filled (6): Score 0 if you have one, 5 for two or three, 10 for four or five, or 15 if you have six. Maple Bar (2): Score 3 points if you have more than six types of donuts. Plain (7): Score 1 point. If you have the most plain donuts, score 3 additional points. If it’s a tie, each tied player gets 1 bonus point. Powdered (4): Score 3 points. 3 Players Boston Cream (6): Score 0 if you have one, 6 for two, 0 for three, 15 for four, 0 for five, or 25 if you have six. Double Chocolate (2): Immediately draw two cards from the deck, choose one to place in front of you and put the other back on top. Red Velvet (2): Score -2 points. Also, take one donut of your choice from the discard pile. Sprinkled (2): Score 2 points. Also, give one of your cards to an opponent. If you have no other cards, you must give this card. 4 Players Bear Claw (2):Score -2 points at the end of the game. Also, take a card from an opponent if possible. Cinnamon Twist (2): Score 1 point. Also, all players pass a card to the left player. If any players have no cards, discard this card. Coffee (2): Score 1 point for each card that gives you negative points. The negative point cards stay negative. Day-Old Donuts (1): Score -7 points. Take up to any 3 cards of your choice from the discard pile. Milk (1): Score 5 points at the end of the game. Also, discard 3 of your cards, or discard this card. Old Fashioned (2): Score 5 points if you have fewer than 10 donut cards. 5 to 6 Players Maple Frosted (2): Score 5 points if you have the fewest cards. Mucho Matcha (2): Score 3 points if you have fewer than 7 types of donuts. Raspberry Frosted (2): Discard one of your previously collected cards. If you have no other cards, you must discard this card. Strawberry Glazed (2): Score -2 points. Also, discard one card of your choice from an opponent. If all opponents have no cards, just keep this card. Board Game Arena would like to thank Gamewright for making it possible to have this

---

Go Nuts for Donuts is a fast-paced card game for the whole family with just a sprinkle of strategy. Outsmart your opponents and collect donuts hot out of the oven for points. But beware, if two players go after the same donut, then no one gets it!

In Go Nuts for Donuts, players lay out donuts from the deck equal to the amount of players plus one. Each player has a number card for each donut that is out. Players all pick a donut they want by placing one of their number cards face down on the table. Players simultaneously reveal their number. If two or more players have matching numbers, that donut is discarded and no one gets it. If you're the only player that bid for the donut, than you take it and place it face up in front of you. Collect sets, unique and powerful donuts, and pairs of donuts to maximize points.

Contents
70 donut cards (full-size cards with brown backs)

        Eclair (3)

        Plain (7) Note that there was a misprint in the 2017 rules incorrectly stating the total of Plain donuts to be only 6.
        Powdered (4)
        French Cruller (1 teal)



    Pink



        Boston Cream (6)
        Double Chocolate (2)
        Red Velvet (2)
        Sprinkled (2)
        French Cruller (1 pink)



    Purple



        Bear Claw (2)
        Cinnamon Twist (2)
        Coffee (2)
        Day Old Donuts (1)
        Milk (1)
        Old Fashioned (2)
        French Cruller (1 purple)



    Blue



        Maple Frosted (2)
        Mucho Matcha (2)
        Raspberry Frosted (2)
        Strawberry Glazed (2)
        French Cruller (1 blue)


42 selection cards

    six sets of miniature cards with white backs. Fronts display the numerals 1 through 7


7 donut row indicators

    cardboard chits with numerals 1 through 7
community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] The worst trick taking game I have ever played in which there is a card that the losing player of the group can decided to use on the winning player to destroy their entire game, king making whom they choose. This is one of the best games to play if you want people to hate tabletop and everyone in the room a total disgrace that this game exists, it doesnt even deserve a slot on this website.

[Rating: 1/10] Very light blind bidding game with set collection. If you bid the same as others then you miss out so there is a bit of the GOPs strategy in this but ultimately not enough for repeat plays. I would go with Sushi Go for a casual audience or Fairy Tale for something heavier.

[Rating: 1/10] Waste of time. Too random, attacks feel bad, takes too long. Play sushi go instead.

[Rating: 2/10] A simultaneous action selection to collect sets game. Very fast and light. Unfortunately, there is also little opportunity for bluffing or sussing out what an opponent is going for, making the decisions mostly nonsense. The simultaneous selection mechanic works well, but not here. Strongly recommend Crossing for a similar and more successful feel of the same style.

[Rating: 2/10] It's a game that is only good for maybe 5 games total. The bidding mechanic feels like random after a few playthroughs, in fact it became less frustrating to just let a dice determine which card I was going to bid for each time. The game could have been better if there was a wider variety of donuts, but in each game you get to see every single card, just in a slightly different order.  Sushi Go Party! by the same publisher is a far better game with a similar aesthetic.

[Rating: 2/10] Simultaneous secret action selection with some take that. You could attempt to bluff and double-think, but it's more likely that you're just gonna get hosed now and again. Get hosed less than everyone else and you win. Hooray!

[Rating: 2/10] This has too much possibility for you to miss out on multiple turns in a row, and too much take-that in the effect of some of the cards, for me to really consider it a very good game. However, I have had a bit of a laugh playing it a handful of times with the right group.

[Rating: 2/10] unfortunately the only fun cards come out in 5+ player counts, which is the absolute worst way to play this game. This game is only for people who will not play any other games.
